name: Tax Scenarios — Roll Forward, Drop One-Time Gain, Layer a Roth Conversion
query: Roll them forward to 2026 — and the $42,500 in gains last year was a one-off, so leave it out. [later] Now layer a $200k Roth conversion on top of that 2026 picture — what does it cost them?
expected_behavior: Step 1: Reads the 2025 filed figures (get_lookback_report or get_extraction_form) to confirm the exact one-time gain amount rather than trusting the advisor's rounded figure blindly
Step 2: Calls model_tax_scenario with baselineYear 2025, targetYear 2026, and a change netting out the $42,500 long-term gain
Step 3: Reports both the 2025 filed figure and the 2026 rolled-forward figure, with the difference
Step 4: On the follow-up, calls model_tax_scenario again with the same baseline/target plus an added roth_conversion_taxable change of 200000
Step 5: Reports the conversion's cost as a delta against the 2026 baseline just built, not a bare new number
success_criteria: changeBy on the one-time-gain change is negative (a reduction), never a new total
targetYear (2026) is explicitly distinct from baselineYear (2025) in both calls
The Roth conversion answer states the dollar difference against the prior 2026 result, e.g. '$X more than the 2026 picture we just built'
Every rate mentioned carries its dollar tax and income basis
No blended federal+state rate percentage appears
must_not: rolling the $42,500 gain forward into 2026 without it being asked about
presenting the Roth conversion's cost as a bare new total with no baseline comparison
any tool name or field path in advisor-facing text
a claim that either scenario was saved or persisted
